title: Glasgow surname and research-study newspaper records
scope: Irish pre-1800 priority search completed for the documented accessible result sets: broad surname queries, catalogue-led quoted names and abbreviations, and bounded spelling checks. Supplemental worldwide quoted-name and Glascow audits are recorded. Every confirmed pre-1800 page has an inline clipping. The 1800–1850 Irish extension remains in progress.
conclusion: Original-verified Glasgow/Glasco/Glascow surname passages are retained with source links, approved excerpts and role-specific profile assessments. Identical readings share a card while every issue remains available. Documentary family statements are distinguished from uncertain existing-profile identities. The recorded pre-1800 priority queries are closed; later coverage is still being completed.
limitations: Coverage is a record of the named queries, provider collections, dates, loaded cards and actually screened positions. OCR omissions, name variants, unavailable titles and gaps in surviving holdings prevent a literal claim to every newspaper mention.

A highlighted Glasgow can be a city, a vessel, a see, a military unit or another person’s address. Only inspected personal-surname passages are treated as surname evidence; clear preview dismissals are not full-page original exclusions.

Original image, provider index/entity label and viewer OCR are different evidence. Viewer No matches can occur despite a printed name, as in the 1798 Secretary chest proclamation. Entity crime labels alone do not prove the name, a perpetrator or a conviction.

Issue dates/pages normally follow provider metadata; checked printed masthead ranges and notice datelines are preserved separately. The 1793 Ordnance heading dates 25 and 27 September differ in parallel reports. No invented commission day or silently corrected year is supplied.

Repeated advertisements and parallel archive scans are grouped by reading, with every issue/excerpt linked. They are not independent events or corroboration. Private-sale, adjournment and judicial-sale stages retain their distinct terms; offers do not establish completed transfers, bankruptcy or death.

Approved inline PNGs are faithful bounded source pixels. Faded text and scan/fold damage remain visible and qualified; fuller parallel excerpts and originals remain linked. No full private viewer capture, reconstructed image or private browser state is published.

Profile matches are confirmed, probable, possible or unlikely as individually assessed. Same name/locality, absent fields or a tree-only parent link do not identify a person. Uncertain before dates are upper bounds; estimated dates are not exact exclusions.

An explicit documentary father–son statement does not identify either existing WikiTree profile. Postal addressees may be deceased; vessel William does not supply its master’s forename. Military selection or appointment reports do not prove completed service; allegations and proclamations retain their attribution.

Core Irish pre-1800 displayed queries and promising original leads are closed; the separate 1800–1850 ledger still has unloaded tails, unreviewed alternates and catalogue name-form gaps. No later-period completeness or live WikiTree relationship upgrade is claimed.

rows.reading: At Dunlop-house, on the 22d ult. Robert Glasgow of Montgreenan, Esq. to Miss Rachel Dunlop, daughter of the late John Dunlop of Dunlop, Esq.

profile_matches.basis: Name, distinctive estate designation and chronology agree with the checked Montgreenan account.

rows.reading: Game licences and deputations issued by the Sheriff Clerk of Ayrshire: Glasgow, Robert, Esq. of Montgreenan. A gamekeeper deputation also names Robert Glasgow of Montgreenan as principal.

profile_matches.basis: Name, distinctive estate designation and chronology agree with the checked Montgreenan account.

rows.reading: County of Ayr, Ayr, 13 January 1808: Robert Morris of Craig, for himself, and as authorised by Mr. Glasgow of Montgreenan.
rows.assessment: The county meeting debated trial by jury in civil cases. Montgreenan’s Glasgow was represented by an authorised attendee; this does not place him physically at the meeting. Name, estate and chronology fit Robert-1076.

profile_matches.basis: Name, distinctive estate designation and chronology agree with the checked Montgreenan account.

rows.reading: At Rome, on the 22d ult. Mrs Robertson Glasgow, of Montgreenan, of a daughter.
rows.assessment: Reports a daughter born 22 November 1827 at Rome. Exact date, place and family designation support Charlotte Glasgow-3003’s recorded birth, but the notice does not give the child’s forename or the mother’s forename. Anne-2874 is the checked Montgreenan succession wife.

rows.reading: County of Antrim: List of Persons applying to Register their Freeholds, under 10 Geo. IV, cap. 8. No. 2324: Alex. Glasgow, Lisnagaver — Lands — Kilconway, townland of Lisnagaver.
rows.assessment: Original page now inspected; replaces the earlier access-blocked heading/extract assessment. This is an application, not proof of admission. No age or relative is stated. Alexander-951 and older Alexander-3904 remain compatible; conflicting age estimates prevent an automatic identification. The property is Lisnagaver; Kilconway is the barony.

profile_matches.basis: Lisnagaver fits; conflicting age estimates leave two compatible Alexanders.
The older Alexander also fits; this notice states no age or relatives.

rows.reading: Hugh Allan v. Trustees of Robert Glasgow: the report calls Mrs Robertson Glasgow the late Robert’s natural daughter and first heir under his 1818 entail. It reports his death in 1827 and a supplementary entail and trust dated 23 June 1821, involving Seafield near Ayr.
rows.assessment: Contemporary account of the 25 August hearing, independently supporting Anne’s daughter/heir description and the 1827 death year. It does not verify 19 April. Hugh Allan-8034, the profile-defined nephew, is a compatible appellant candidate; older Allan-8028 has no death recorded but would be 109. Neither identity is proved. These later deeds are distinct from the uninspected 1803 trust.

rows.reading: House of Lords appeals: the report reproduces clauses of Glasgow’s settlement and says Lord Brougham recommended reversing the judgment below; judgment reversed accordingly. The heading appears to read Henry Allen v. Trustees of R. Glasgow.
rows.assessment: Reports the Wednesday judgment, 2 September 1835. The estate, Seafield dispute and counsel identify the same litigation as the 26 August report, whose appellant is Hugh Allan. Preserve the discrepant heading; compare the original court papers before resolving the name. Reported deed extracts are not an inspection of the original deed.

rows.reading: Shocking catastrophe at Rasharkin: Robt. Glasgow, described as a neighbour at Lisnagaver, warned James M’Caughern about a dangerous gable before it fell; Glasgow narrowly escaped while leaving the doorway and raised the alarm.
rows.assessment: Genuine Glasgow surname in a local incident. Robert-938 and Robert-3449 remain compatible candidates; no age, parents, occupation or link to a valuation holding is stated. A later Scottish death does not exclude Robert-938 being in Ireland in 1861.

rows.reading: Auction advertised for 22 September at the Donegall Arms, Belfast: Larne corn and wheat mills, Kilwaughter corn mill, and Inver flour mills, with machinery, lands and lease interests in James Holmes & Co.’s possession.
rows.assessment: Place-study evidence only. Different mill interests were held under the heirs of the Marquis of Antrim and under the Marquis of Donegall. The passage names no Glasgow surname and does not connect the Glasgow families to these mills or to a seventeenth-century glassworks.

rows.assessment: Identified as Glasgow-3896 by name, place and exact death date. The prior both-73 reading was corrected by original-capture review on 4 October 2026. No kin or parents stated.

profile_matches.basis: Name, Church Street, Kilrea and exact 16 October 1871 death date agree; newspaper ages differ.

rows.reading: Wm. Glasgow, master of brig William; Bordeaux voyage. A separate cargo advertisement says the William, Capt. Glasgow, arrived from Bourdeaux for Hugh Crawford & Co.; that notice is dated Belfast, 3 December 1792. James Hamill advertises French apples, almonds and other goods arrived per the William, Captain Glasgow, from Bordeaux; notice dated 7 December 1792.
rows.assessment: Same vessel and named master; household still unproved. Two separate notices on this page are preserved inline; the captain/master identification remains the existing qualified shipping cluster. Separate cargo passage preserved inline; These notices name the vessel William and Captain Glasgow; no captain forename is stated in them. Independently inspected 1792 sailing advertisements explicitly name Wm./William Glasgow as master of the same brig, supporting probable continuity. Vessel names and voyage ports do not establish personal residence or kinship. Long-s typography is normalized to s.

profile_matches.basis: Larne maritime candidate remains unresolved; the named 1792 master supplies the forename, while these cargo notices state captain surname only. Same brig and routes support probable continuity, not proved identity.

rows.reading: William Glasgow, Kildress delegate and subsequent chairman; meeting 16 January 1793.
rows.assessment: Candidate Glasgow-2915; no father or wife in notice.

rows.reading: Captain Glasgow of brig William returned from Petersburg with hemp and flax.
rows.assessment: Surname is the captain’s name; William is the vessel. Captain forename unstated; continuity with the named 1792 master is probable, not proved. Original page-1 masthead reads: No. 420. From Thursday, January 7, to Monday, January 11, 1796. The indexed issue date is the beginning of that printed range; the later advertisement date lies within it. Preserve the printed range without inferring a separate issue day.

rows.reading: William Glasgow died 21 January at Sandusky City, Ohio, age 55; formerly Killycurragh near Cookstown; ruling elder at First Cookstown before emigration.
rows.assessment: Identified as Glasgow-1675. Preserve News-Letter age 55 alongside attributed Mercury age 56; not living uncle in 1858.

profile_matches.basis: Sandusky death, Killycurragh origin and First Cookstown connection agree; preserve the reported 55/56 age discrepancy.

rows.reading: William Glasgow Esq., Cookstown, retired from business; presentation at Imperial Hotel, Belfast, 1 January: silver ewer and cake basket.
rows.assessment: Retired merchant Glasgow-3814 is a strong compatible candidate; kinship to 1858 partners remains unproved.

profile_matches.basis: Age, locality and merchant trade fit; the later senior-uncle identity is still unproved.

rows.reading: The named witness Benjamin Glasgow identifies the late Robert Glasgow as his father, says he managed his father’s mill from 1850, and dates Robert’s death to 1856. Benjamin’s evidence describes a companion as “witness’s uncle, Mr. Glasgow, sen.”; identification as William belongs to the separate case context, not this quotation.
rows.assessment: Certain documentary father–son relationship; identification of Robert with Glasgow-2656 or Glasgow-3941 remains qualified. Counsel’s reference to Robert’s sons supports a qualified brother inference for co-plaintiff William. The uncle’s paternal or maternal side and all mothers are unstated. No parents are established for John Glasgow-2058.

prior_assessment.assessment: Two distinct Williams. Robert is father of singular present plaintiff, unspecified between Benjamin and William. Does not prove parents of John-2058.

Recorded 1831 death is uncertain. If correct, it conflicts with the witness’s 1856 father-death statement; compare original records.

rows.assessment: Confirms same named partners; no ages or additional parental identification.

rows.reading: Tin Tenement, Main Street, and Monrush town parks for sale at Cookstown; apply to Mr William Glasgow, Cookstown; notice dated 15 August 1861.
rows.assessment: Unassigned same-name contact. No kinship or proof that William owned the entire property.

rows.reading: House occupied by Joseph M’Cormick, formerly residence of late Robert Glasgow; apply to Benjamin and William Glasgow, Drapersfield Mills, Cookstown; notice dated 16 January.
rows.assessment: Partners named. The former occupant Robert died before 16 January 1864, but identity with 1842 partner still requires a bridge.

rows.reading: Cheque for £71 12s 7d drawn by Benjamin and William Glasgow in favour of John Finlay junior, mentioned in William Adair case.
rows.assessment: Business partnership confirmed; age and relatives unstated. William Adair is another person.

rows.reading: Benjamin Glasgow Esq., Drapersfield, Cookstown, contact for Eary House and lands auction, estate of late William Magee.
rows.assessment: Contact, not explicitly executor. Matches the documented Drapersfield business context.

rows.reading: Benjamin Glasgow Esq., of Drapersfield, granted use of a field for the 12 July Cookstown gathering.
rows.assessment: Later identity control: current action after Benjamin-2059’s February death strongly distinguishes the two Benjamins.

profile_matches.basis: Died 8 February 1870, before the reported July 1870 action; retained as a comparison only.
Chronology fits; trade and family identity remain unproved.

rows.reading: William Treacy, second son of Robert Treacy, married Emma, daughter of late William Alexander Glasgow, 4 September, St Thomas’s Church, Belfast; both of Parsonstown.
rows.assessment: Later family lead, outside pre-1870 publication window. William groom is Treacy, not Glasgow.

rows.reading: Master Benjamin Glasgow of Cookstown is listed for one shilling towards support of scholars in the agricultural school in June 1850.
rows.assessment: A donor list, not proof that Benjamin attended the school. “Master” supplies no exact age. Benjamin-2059 (reported born about 1835) and Benjamin-2566 (about 1840) are compatible young catalogue namesakes; assignment to either, or to the Drapersfield Benjamin, is unresolved. The surgeon who died in 1833 is excluded.
